A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gromov-Monge Gap research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic transport experiments, disentanglement results on four image datasets, gradient-stability analyses, and decoder-free experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds entropy-sensitivity experiments, higher-resolution Shapes3D results, and latent-traversal visualizations.

M1.justification: The GMG definition, training objectives, Algorithm 1, and Appendix E implementation remain unchanged. For the added 128 × 128 experiment, v3 Appendix D.4 explicitly adds one decoder layer, a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: The four original image datasets and synthetic transport tasks are retained. Appendix D.4 adds evaluation with Shapes3D upscaled to 128 × 128, extending the tested input-resolution conditions without introducing a new domain or generative-factor population.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same β-VAE, β-TCVAE, HFS, DST, and Jacobian-regularization configurations. The added resolution experiment evaluates existing base models with and without GMG; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: v3 adds a six-value entropy-scale sweep with solver-iteration measurements over the first three epochs, a focused hyperparameter grid for 128 × 128 images, and latent traversals from −1 to 1 using selected best-performing runs. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The entropy experiment's dataset is inconsistently identified as DSprites in Appendix D.3 and SmallNORB in Figure 5.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3–D.5 substantially expand the supplementary validation: they test sensitivity to entropy strength and its computational consequences, examine scaling to higher image resolution, and visualize whether individual latent dimensions isolate factors. Existing cost-function, encoder/decoder, gradient-stability, and decoder-free analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The retained quantitative tables preserve their five-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting. The added solver study also specifies five seeds; no increase in repeated runs, new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1, 2, and 4, and v2 Table 5/v3 Table 7, are unchanged. New Table 6 reports 128 × 128 results, including β-VAE scores of 54.3 ± 19.3 without GMG and 63.9 ± 8.2 with decoder GMG. Figure 5 adds entropy-response and iteration curves; the traversal captions add selected-run scores, and Section 4.2 reports approximately 3 milliseconds per GMG batch.

T1.justification: The original definitions, propositions, weak-convexity theorem, and Appendix B proofs are retained apart from renumbering. Appendix D.3 newly states an epsilon log(1/epsilon) entropic approximation-error bound attributed to Zhang et al. (2023), including its cost conditions and dependence on dimensions and fourth moments.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: GMG as a geometric regularizer, integration with prior-matching objectives, weak-convexity guarantees, and improved disentanglement across four benchmarks. Condensing the introduction's contribution list does not change these claims, which remain in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation of entropy strength as a sharpness parameter, contrasting its influence on a training loss with its influence on directly predicted transport maps. It also interprets the new experiments as supporting practical entropy robustness and resolution scalability. The existing limitation that DST can outperform GMG without a decoder remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-repository link, Algorithm 2 detailing the existing entropic GW solver, the higher-resolution decoder adaptation and search grid, and a per-batch runtime estimate. The implementation listing, original architecture and training details, and RTX 2080TI disclosure were already present in v2.

R1.justification: v3 removes the dedicated Neural GW comparison and several associated references, while adding quadratic-OT history and literature on entropy and gap regularization. Its discussion of concurrent Sotiropoulou and Alvarez-Melis work drops the assertion that they do not investigate GMG properties, retaining the distinction concerning disentanglement applications.

P1.justification: The distortion material moves from v2 Section 3.1 into v3 Section 2.3, with corresponding subsection and theorem renumbering. Background paragraphs are rewritten, experimental prose is condensed, and headers change to ICLR 2025 publication status. Most remaining text and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a two-panel entropy/performance and iteration plot, two latent-traversal image grids, higher-resolution hyperparameter and results tables, and a solver pseudocode display. These substantially expand the visual evidence. Existing displays are retained; the decoder-free table moves from Table 5 to Table 7.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens empirical validation and usability through entropy-sensitivity and convergence checks, higher-resolution evaluation, latent visualizations, and additional solver and code-access information. The original results and proofs are preserved. The gains are limited by the use of upscaled existing data and selected best-run visualizations, while the DSprites/SmallNORB mismatch between Appendix D.3 and Figure 5 leaves the new sensitivity experiment's dataset uncertain.
